slides.title: Module 4: Convolutional Neural Networks
points: How convolution, pooling, architectural priors, variants, structured outputs, data types, efficient algorithms, and CNN history explain modern visual deep learning.
slides.takeaway: How convolution, pooling, architectural priors, variants, structured outputs, data types, efficient algorithms, and CNN history explain modern visual deep learning.

slides.title: Module 4 begins with convolution, pooling, and priors
Module 4 then connects CNNs to outputs, data, efficiency, and history
A convolution applies the same small filter across many locations
points: Operation
A kernel slides over an input array. At each location, it multiplies local input values by kernel weights and sums the result.
Output
The repeated operation produces a feature map that marks where the learned pattern appears.
slides.takeaway: A kernel slides over an input array. At each location, it multiplies local input values by kernel weights and sums the result.

slides.title: The convolution operation is a weighted local sum
points: S(i, j) = Σm Σn I(i+m, j+n) K(m, n)
I is the input array.
K is the convolution kernel or filter.
S is the output feature map at location (i, j).
slides.takeaway: S is the output feature map at location (i, j).
slides.formula: S(i, j) = Σm Σn I(i+m, j+n) K(m, n)

slides.title: CNN motivation starts with three useful assumptions
points: Locality
Nearby values are usually more related than distant values.
Parameter sharing
The same feature may be useful at many positions.
Translation equivariance
Moving the input moves the feature response.
extraPoints: Small features combine into larger patterns across layers.
slides.takeaway: Nearby values are usually more related than distant values.

slides.title: Convolution dramatically reduces parameters compared with dense layers
points: Dense connection
Every input position can have a different weight into every output unit, which becomes expensive for images.
Convolutional connection
A small kernel is shared across spatial locations, reducing parameter count and improving sample efficiency.
slides.takeaway: Every input position can have a different weight into every output unit, which becomes expensive for images.

slides.title: Convolution and pooling act as an infinitely strong prior
points: Prior from convolution
The network assumes useful features are local and that the same feature detector should be reused across positions.
Prior from pooling
The network assumes exact feature position may matter less than whether the feature appears in a local region.
slides.takeaway: The network assumes useful features are local and that the same feature detector should be reused across positions.

slides.title: A strong prior helps when the data match the assumption
points: Helpful case
For images, edges and textures can appear at many locations, so shared filters and pooling are useful assumptions.
Risky case
If location-specific patterns are essential, too much sharing or pooling can remove information the task needs.
slides.takeaway: For images, edges and textures can appear at many locations, so shared filters and pooling are useful assumptions.

slides.title: Structured outputs predict more than one class label

A CNN maps an input image to one label, such as cat, car, or digit.
Structured output
A CNN may output a spatial map, sequence, bounding boxes, masks, or multiple labels aligned to the input.

slides.title: Data layout changes how convolution is implemented
points: Shape matters
The same conceptual operation may be organized as channels-first, channels-last, batched tensors, or tiled memory layouts.
Hardware matters
Efficient CNN implementations arrange data to reduce memory movement and exploit parallel matrix or tensor operations.

slides.title: Efficiency depends on kernel size, feature-map size, and hardware
points: Small kernels such as 3 x 3 are common because they are expressive and efficient.
Large feature maps make memory movement a major cost.
Batches let hardware reuse computation patterns.
The best algorithm can change across CPU, GPU, mobile, and accelerator settings.
slides.takeaway: Small kernels such as 3 x 3 are common because they are expressive and efficient.

slides.title: The history of CNNs is also a history of scale
points: The core ideas are older than the modern deep learning boom.
Large labeled datasets made supervised visual learning more useful.
GPU computation made deeper and wider CNN training practical.
Architectural refinements improved trainability, accuracy, and efficiency.

Pooling

Variants

extraPoints: Implementation matters because convolution dominates computation.
